beats.headline: Alphabet drops 3.85% amid quiet peer trading
beats.explanation: Alphabet fell 3.85% to close at $290.44 on 1.5x average volume with no company-specific news reported. The drop appeared company-specific, as supplier Apple edged up 0.06%, competitor Intel gained 0.11%, and competitor Nvidia slipped just 0.25%.

beats.headline: Shares surge 9.96% following 10-Q and 8-K filings
beats.explanation: Alphabet surged 9.96% to $384.80 on 2.9x average volume following the submission of an 8-K on April 29 and a 10-Q on April 30. The rally was company-specific, standing in contrast to competitor Nvidia, which dropped 4.63%, and competitor Intel, which dipped 0.28%.

beats.headline: Alphabet falls 3.03% on 8-K filing date
beats.explanation: Alphabet declined 3.03% to $388.64 on 1.2x average volume on the day it submitted an 8-K filing. The drop was company-specific, diverging from competitors Intel and Nvidia, which advanced 3.62% and 1.97% respectively.

beats.headline: Alphabet drops 3.86% without company news
beats.explanation: Alphabet shares slipped 3.86% to $361.85 on 2.0x average volume with no company-specific announcements. The decline was largely company-specific, as supplier Apple rose 2.90%, while competitors Intel and Nvidia recorded smaller losses of 1.28% and 0.69%.

beats.headline: Alphabet climbs 3.68% following 8-K filing
beats.explanation: Alphabet climbed 3.68% to $372.19 on 1.8x average volume on the same day it submitted an 8-K filing. The positive momentum was partly shared with competitor Nvidia, which gained 1.82%, and supplier Apple, which added 0.31%, while competitor Intel fell 0.82%.

beats.headline: Alphabet drops 4.99% as Intel rallies
beats.explanation: Alphabet shares lost 4.99% to close at $349.68 on 2.1x average volume with no news released. The pullback was company-specific, contrasting with a 5.19% rally in competitor Intel and milder declines in supplier Apple (-0.34%) and competitor Nvidia (-0.97%).

beats.headline: Alphabet rises 4.82% alongside chip competitors
beats.explanation: Alphabet advanced 4.82% to $353.65 on 1.4x average volume without company-specific news. The advance was shared with competitors Intel and Nvidia, which gained 2.65% and 1.27% respectively, whereas supplier Apple dropped 0.72%.

beats.headline: Shares sink 7.13% after Q2 filings
beats.explanation: Alphabet fell 7.13% to $317.69 on 2.8x average volume following the submission of an 8-K on July 22 and a 10-Q on July 23. While peers also retreated—competitors Intel and Nvidia fell 2.33% and 1.56%, and supplier Apple fell 1.30%—Alphabet's move was notably more pronounced.

beats.headline: Alphabet jumps 6.73% while Apple falls
beats.explanation: Alphabet gained 6.73% to $356.13 on 1.9x average volume without new company filings. The rebound was company-specific, sharply diverging from supplier Apple's 7.35% drop and competitor Intel's 1.02% dip, though competitor Nvidia rose 2.93%.

beats.headline: Alphabet gains 4.88% continuing rebound
beats.explanation: Alphabet increased 4.88% to $373.51 on 1.6x average volume in the absence of company-specific headlines. Competitors Nvidia and Intel also traded higher, gaining 2.93% and 0.89% respectively, while supplier Apple fell 1.78%.

beats.headline: Alphabet drops 4.03% against rising peers
beats.explanation: Alphabet dropped 4.03% to $362.43 on 1.9x average volume with no company news reported. The selloff was company-specific, running counter to competitor Nvidia's 3.44% gain, competitor Intel's 0.20% rise, and supplier Apple's 0.52% increase.

beats.headline: Alphabet gains 3.22% while chip peers drop
beats.explanation: Alphabet rose 3.22% to $349.39 on 1.5x average volume without accompanying company disclosures. The gain was company-specific, diverging from competitors Intel and Nvidia, which dropped 5.59% and 3.36% respectively, while supplier Apple edged up 0.24%.

arc: Between March and September 2026, Alphabet experienced a volatile series of moves characterized by sharp filing-driven repricings and frequent decoupling from its technology peers. The stock's largest single-day surge arrived on April 30, when it jumped 9.96% to $384.80 following its Q1 10-Q and 8-K filings, but it later endured a steep 7.13% decline to $317.69 around its Q2 filings on July 23. Throughout the summer, Alphabet frequently exhibited company-specific swings that diverged from key connected companies—such as competitor Nvidia and supplier Apple—highlighting that idiosyncratic catalysts and post-earnings adjustments were the primary drivers of trading action over the period.
